title: Chess, But My Knights Can MATE
summary: Chess vs Stockfish where White's knights are 'horses' that breed: whenever a knight move ends adjacent to another friendly knight, a new white knight spawns on an empty square adjacent to them (random). Narrator develops only knights, sacrifices horses knowing new ones keep spawning, wins the queen before move 10, challenges himself to move only knights, and checkmates with a cloud of horses.
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600). Only White's knights breed.
When a white knight moves to a square adjacent (8-neighbour) to another white knight, a new white knight spawns on a random empty square adjacent to the pair/the moved knight.
Moves that don't end adjacent to another knight spawn nothing (e.g. a capture with check far away).
No cap on number of knights mentioned (legacy cap 6 is wrong) [inferred].
Spawns can accidentally stalemate the opponent; keep at least two knights to keep breeding.
win_condition: Checkmate Stockfish (narrator did it moving only knights).
